milestones.title: Irrationality of gamma (the weaker open target)
milestones.milestone_description: Whether Euler's constant is rational is itself unsettled. Transcendence implies it, so it sits below the mission goal, but a proof of irrationality alone would already resolve a problem open since Euler.

milestones.title: Reduction — irrationality from vanishing linear forms
milestones.milestone_description: The classical criterion converting irrationality into the construction of integer sequences $(p_n, q_n)$ with $q_n\gamma - p_n \to 0$ and never zero. Elementary and provable now; it is the entry point of the mission and the shape all known attacks take.

milestones.title: Aptekarev — at least one of $\gamma$, $\delta$ is irrational
milestones.milestone_description: The strongest unconditional irrationality statement known, resting on simultaneous Pade approximation to the pair of functions behind $\gamma$ and the Euler–Gompertz constant, after Mahler and Shidlovskii. The disjunction cannot presently be split.

milestones.title: Rivoal — at least one of $\gamma$, $\delta$ is transcendental
milestones.milestone_description: Rivoal's upgrade of the disjunction from rationality to algebraicity, obtained by running the approximation argument against arbitrary algebraic numbers. Marks the current boundary of Diophantine approximation for these constants.

milestones.title: Brent–McMillan and Papanikolaou — denominator bound
milestones.milestone_description: If $\gamma = p/q$ then $q > 10^{244663}$, by continued-fraction analysis of a high-precision computation. A measurement of how far computation reaches, not a step toward a proof; included so the dependency graph is truthful about what is known.
